Results.ReviewText: We had bought this grill about 9 months ago, the first few months it was hardly used due to winter. From the beginning the grill did not cook evenly, the temperature was much lower in the front than the back, which is not what you want when spending this kind of money on a "smaller" grill. It got much worse though, around spring we started to use it more, and one day cooking steaks it had caught fire, to the point where we needed a fire extinguisher to put it out. At first due to the severity we thought it was maybe a propane leak either from the tank or lines, or maybe improper assembly. But after we deep cleaned the grill we tested everywhere and could find no leaks. Literally the next time grill, or time after, the same thing occurred. This time we caught it faster but still had to use an abundance of baking soda to stop it, again requiring a deep clean. Pretty much every other time we have used this grill since then it occurs, the last time causing the damage in the pictures attached, and the grill peaked a temp at over 600 degrees. We noticed that for whatever reason the small amounts of grease and debris are being ignited and catching whatever other material is in the bottom of the grill and grease pan on fire, hence it being hard to put out. BUT with having owned a few BBQs in the past, since when does a whole BBQ catch on fire due to a little grease and debris? It is a grill, it's purpose is to get down and dirty and produce good food, not require a deep clean after every use. The pictures should show how clean it is and still it ignites... Well while at the store the other day we had noticed the grill had a new design change both on external looks but also the internal design, pretty sure this isn't a coincidence... This isn't a cheap grill for the size, one would say on the higher end even, but after this experience we will never buy a Weber again.
Results.Title: Waste of money, disappointed. You were warned...

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)

We have BBQed hamburgers, steak, pork loin chops, chicken, pineapple, all kinds of vegetables and steak fries. Everything was awesome. This grill is so easy to use we will probably become year round BBQers.

When the 154 lb carton arrived and we started unpacking the quality parts and well organized packaging were obvious.  After sorting out and checking off all the various parts we started assembly which required about an hour as he knew what the finished grill would look like.  The pictorial instructions and marked fastener packages made assembly intuitive and easy.  Despite the packaging one of the legs was received twisted and bent and required work with persuasive tools to straighten it. 
We attached the propane tank and it fired up immediately.  
Grills food fast , evenly and easy to keep clean.

The heavy, bulky carton needs die cut handholds on each side to reduce damage during the journey  from factory to customer.  It is very hard to handle off the truck and probably just dumped off the tailgate resulting in damage to the contents.
Results.Title: Well designed quality grill

Results.ReviewText:
Had it a couple months now and overall satisfied at this time.  Two concerns I have. 1). Weber why would you design a grill that must be lifted up on one side to utilize the wheels to move the grill without a lift point/handles. Critical design flaw. Not to mention just common sense. 2.) while the grill does get to 500 F it takes a little more time than it should. While it’s summer now and warm, I have serious reservations how well this grill will maintain heat in colder weather. 

Pulled a star for design and another due to the slow heating characteristics.   If this grill performs in colder weather I will probably change to 4 stats but I want to see it actually perform first in the four seasons as my previous grill always did.

Results.ReviewText:
I bought an E-310 to replace a worn out Weber kettle. The gas grill is easy to use, and the porcelain coated grates are very simple to keep clean with a stainless steel wire brush. The replaceable drip pan is a nice feature.

Overall this is a nice unit. I docked one star because of the folding tray which doubles as a handle for moving the unit around. This feature is poorly engineered and will eventually become too loose to properly lock in place. It can be fixed by removing the two standoff nuts and replacing them with a 1 inch fender washer, a locking washer, and a 7/8 inch nut. While it will then no longer fold down without removing the nuts, the tray will then function properly as a handle without slippage.

Results.ReviewText: We bought this grill because our other one, which we had to repair twice, finally died. We have owned small, charcoal Weber grills in the past and felt it was time to buy a gas grill. The Spirit II has all the features we wanted: a way to tell if the supply tank is running low, a temperature gauge, it's easy to move, outstanding warranty, and it looks fine (we opted for the red hood). Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: I have always owned fairly inexpensive grills from big box stores, thinking that Weber grills were overpriced and you were mostly paying for the name. My previous grill was mostly stainless steel, had tons of features, and was very nice...when new. After 4 years of ownership, it was not so nice anymore. The electric starter lasted for exactly one season, the vaporizoer/flavorizer/whatever bars were rotting away, the grates were getting harder to clean, etc. It was clearly time to replace it.  This time, instead of heading to the big box and picking up a mid-priced grill with as many features as I could find, I went online and started reading reviews. I read them on the websites that sold grills, I read articles, basically whatever I could find. And they all said basically the same thing, get a Weber Spirit. Seriously, that's what they said. Just get the Weber Spirit. So I did. Yeah, its costs twice as much as the other grills I've bought, and yeah, it is lacking many features (no side burner, no sear station, etc). But what it is lacking in features, it makes up for in spades in quality. To be honest, at first, I wasn't that impressed with its quality. The metal is of a lower gauge than I expected, maybe the wheels aren't quite what I'd expect. But the first time you actually grill with it.....yup, there's the quality. The evenness of the heat is remarkable. No more moving burgers around to get them to all cook the same. Put as many on there as you want, flip them in place, and they will all be cooked exactly the same. And somehow, they taste better, much better. That must be a byproduct of the evenness, but what I grill tastes much better than it did on my old grill. Abnd with a 10 year warranty, this will be the longest I will ever have a grill, and I couldn't be happier about it. Way to go Weber, you nailed it.
Results.Title: Not a perfect grill, but close
